prerequisites: Reading comprehension in English for scientific-technical texts

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capabilities to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of biomechanics.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical stresses in biological systems
Linear elasticity applied to tissue
Plastic deformation and fracture limits
Viscoelasticity
Mechanical fatigue
Bone tissue: structure, functions, histology and classification
Bone physiology: formation, growth and remodeling processes
Fracture and repair: injury mechanisms and consolidation processes
Biomechanical characterization: bone properties and influencing factors
Experimental methodology: classical mechanical tests and alternative techniques
Classification, structure and types of joints
Articular cartilage: functions, composition, structure
Mechanical properties and behavior of articular cartilage
Lubrication, wear and degeneration
Articular systems: classification, structure and typology
Articular cartilage: functions, composition and structural organization
Mechanical characterization: properties and behavior models of cartilage
Articular tribology: mechanisms of lubrication, wear and degeneration
Composition and organization: characterization of fibrous connective tissue and collagen
Structural architecture: morphological differences between tendon and ligament
Biomechanical response: functional properties and behavior under load
Influencing factors and pathomechanics: determining variables and types of injuries
Mechanical modeling: theoretical approaches and characterization of structures
Fundamentals of biomaterials: concept, historical evolution and general classification
Design and selection criteria: functional requirements and biocompatibility
Clinical applications: repair, substitution and regenerative medicine
Metallic biomaterials: mechanical properties, corrosion and applications in bone fixation
Polymeric biomaterials: synthetic and natural polymers; degradation and applications in soft tissues
Ceramic biomaterials: inert, active and resorbable bioceramics
Fracture pathophysiology: definition and classification criteria
Therapeutic approach: general principles and types of treatment
Fixation and osteosynthesis systems: classification and analysis of devices for consolidation
Fundamentals of constitutive models: typology and application in biological systems
Formulation in solid mechanics: mathematical bases for tissue analysis
Introduction to the Finite Element Method (FEM): application in solving biodynamic problems
teaching_methods: Study of concepts complemented with resolution of practical exercises and problems
Provision of specific software, scripts, and results notebooks for practicals
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 75% from the written exam, 20% from the Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC), and 5% from the practical assignments. The PECs will only be considered if the score on the written exam is equal to or greater than 4 out of 10. Passing the practical assignments is a mandatory requirement to pass the subject. Once the practicals are passed, their score is retained for subsequent academic years. If the exam and PECs are passed but not the practicals, the exam and PEC scores are retained only for resits within the same academic year.
